_comment: Golden `derive_annotation_id` vectors (annotation-cutover design). `derive_annotation_id` (colca_data_contracts.payload, this package) is the one owner of the id-derivation rule: ULID-encode the first 16 bytes of SHA-256(f"{annotation_type_id}|{source}|{time_start:.6f}|{','.join(sorted(signal_ids))}"). The signal set is part of the identity since 2026-09-07 (design §8): the `signal_ids` of every case are hashed sorted, so the two rows that carry the same set in a different order must derive the SAME id, a case with no signals contributes the empty string after the final `|`, and two rows that differ only in their signal set must derive DIFFERENT ids — that last pair is the 409 collision this rule exists to end. plugins/uns/exec_edit_annotation.go needs the identical rule natively in Go (a human-authored annotation command derives its id at the node, never in the API, and plugins/uns is stdlib-only so it cannot import a ULID library or this package). Necessary duplication (architecture principle 2, tier 2), pinned by one checked-in dataset both native copies answer to: this package's tests/test_annotation_payload.py, and colca's plugins/uns/exec_edit_annotation_test.go. A change to either implementation that stops matching these vectors fails on both sides before it ever reaches a producer and a human deriving different ids for the same annotation. `source` values follow whichever author actually stamps them in production: a dataops producer's broker-native AnnotationOutput uses `dataops/{producer.name}` (dataops.outputs.bind_annotation_outputs); a person authoring through the Edit `annotation` intent gets a server-stamped `user/<sub>` and a machine identity gets `service/<client-id>` or `service/<service-name>`. The `api/human:u-franz` row predates the `user/<sub>` convention and is kept only because it is a real pinned regression vector (source is opaque to the Go executor -- unparsed, just hashed); `user/u-franz` alongside it at the same type/time_start is the row that matches what production emits today for a human author.

_sources_comment: Golden `source` vectors per identity KIND (node-side command authorization design): the `source` half of a derived annotation id names the kind of identity that authored it. The rule has two native owners — the API's annotation_source (stamps it on every intent) and plugins/uns AnnotationSource (re-derives it at the executor to prove authorship under an operate grant) — and both must answer these cases: a person (JWT or an API key on that person) -> user/<sub>; a Keycloak service account (preferred_username starts with service-account-) -> service/<client-id>; an mTLS edge.Service -> service/<service-name> (api only: a service is never the Edit executor's actor).
